recipe.name: Cold-fill Moka Express at equipment fill, with first-gurgle stop
equipment: Complete classic aluminum Bialetti Moka Express, such as the 3-cup model
Optional scale to record this pot's fill quantities
recipe.grind_description: Moka-specific grind; coarser than machine espresso and finer than ordinary drip, roughly granulated sugar. Never powder-fine espresso grounds or tamping.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Assembled pot placed on active heat source
expected_time_s.clock_end: Pot removed from heat at first gurgling completion cue

recipe.completion_signal: First gurgling change prompts heat removal; discharge settles and brewed coffee is collected in upper chamber. Keep lid closed during heating on Moka Express. If a different model permits viewing the outlet, pale/bubbly/sputtering flow is an app-authored additional stopping cue.

steps.instruction: Inspect cold pot's gasket, filter plate, funnel and valve for correct placement, cleanliness and damage. Complete the supplied first-use procedure when new; never heat dry.
steps.why: Sound, clear components are prerequisites for controlled pressure and sealing.
steps.completion: All required components intact, clean and properly seated; new-pot commissioning completed.

steps.instruction: Fill lower chamber with cold drinking water just below valve's lower edge; insert funnel. Remove excess if water enters coffee basket.
steps.why: The actual pot's valve level, not a generic ratio, determines reservoir fill.
steps.completion: Valve remains uncovered and basket is not flooded.

steps.instruction: Completely fill basket with loose moka-ground coffee, level gently without pressing, and remove grounds from sealing rim.
steps.why: A clean rim seals properly; packed or excessively fine grounds restrict passage.
steps.completion: Full loose level basket and clean sealing rim.

steps.instruction: Tighten metal sections securely while cold, without excessive force or levering by handle; close lid and orient safety valve away from yourself and others.
steps.why: Correct closure controls leaks; closed lid and valve orientation follow this model's manual and keep a possible steam jet away from people.
steps.completion: Securely assembled pot with closed lid and unobstructed valve directed away from people.

steps.instruction: Place pot stably on compatible active hob; start optional observation clock now. Use controlled low-to-medium heat, with gas flame confined beneath base and handle clear. Stay nearby.
steps.why: Controlled heating avoids forcing rapid delivery and overheating the finished coffee.
steps.completion: Coffee delivery begins; no joint leakage or abnormal valve discharge.

steps.instruction: Remove from heat at the first gurgling change, using handle and heat protection. Keep clear of steam and let remaining discharge settle on a heatproof trivet.
steps.why: This app-authored endpoint follows illy's cue rather than a generic timer or the goal of emptying the reservoir.
steps.completion: Heat removed; active discharge settles. A small boiler residue may remain.

steps.instruction: Once discharge settles, lift lid by knob from a safe position, stir and pour carefully. Allow complete cooling before unscrewing. Rinse aluminum parts with warm water without detergent or abrasives; dry fully and store unclosed.
steps.why: Stirring mixes collected coffee; full cooldown protects against hot metal, liquid and pressure, and compatible care protects aluminum.
steps.completion: Coffee served; completely cool, clean, dry pot ready for storage.

variants.name: Blue Bottle 6-cup hot-start option
variants.how_it_differs: Separate published example of about 20–22 g coffee and approximately 345 g reservoir water, with optional hot filling and medium heat. Quantity remains subordinate to actual valve level; safely protect against the already hot base. It changes warm-up timing and does not make the cold procedure a Blue Bottle recipe. Do not infer exact beverage yield or a universal ratio.

variants.name: Another pot size or stainless/induction model
variants.how_it_differs: Use the pot's own reservoir and basket geometry and approved hob, not linear gram scaling. Classic aluminum Moka Express is not directly induction compatible. Stainless Venus care differs by model/edition/region; read supplied manual before detergent or dishwasher use.

variants.name: Comandante C40 grind example
variants.how_it_differs: App's 14–20-click range matches the manufacturer's stovetop starting range and stated click zero. The app-selected 17-click midpoint is not a published universal optimum; retain model/standard-axle calibration limits and do not transfer to other grinders or Red Clix.

variants.name: Visible-flow cue where another model permits it
variants.how_it_differs: App-authored conservative visual cue: if the supplied manual allows viewing flow, remove heat as flow pales or becomes bubbly/sputtering. It must not override Moka Express's closed-lid instruction. This precise color cue has not been independently verified as a universal maker rule.

troubleshooting.symptom: No coffee, joint leakage or safety-valve venting
troubleshooting.check_first: Turn off heat and cool completely. Check presence/condition/position of parts, valve-limited water fill, clear filter passages, clean rim and sound seal.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Correct assembly or replace damaged parts with compatible maker parts; ensure loose moka-specific grounds. Never force flow by extra heat or open hot. Stop use and contact maker if abnormal venting persists.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check that controlled heat was used and finished coffee was not left boiling.
troubleshooting.adjustment: First reduce heat and remove at initial gurgle; if needed after a repeat, try slightly coarser moka grounds. Taste adjustment is app-authored, not a certain diagnosis.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check full loose basket, intended water level, clear paths and sound seal.
troubleshooting.adjustment: After equipment checks, try a small finer adjustment while remaining coarser than machine espresso. App-authored taste suggestion; never tamp or exceed safe fill.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check whether coffee delivery ended normally without joint leaks or abnormal valve venting.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Small residual water is normal; do not keep heating to empty the boiler. Quantify output on an actual brew if repeatability is needed.

safety: Never heat the pot without water. A manufacturer-prescribed water-filled commissioning/descaling cycle is different from an empty dry run.
Fill below safety valve's lower edge; never cover, block or bypass it. Keep fitted valve maintained according to exact model instructions.
Use moka-specific grounds and a full loose basket; never tamp. Check gasket, filter plate and funnel before heating.
Assemble securely before heat and never use handle as tightening lever. Keep Moka Express lid closed during use and orient safety valve away from yourself and others.
Use compatible stable hob with controlled heat; keep gas flame inside base and handle clear. Stay nearby and keep children away.
If leakage or abnormal valve venting occurs, stop heat and allow cooling; never open hot or force a blockage with extra heat.
Keep face/hands clear of steam and hot coffee. Handle with heat protection and place on heatproof surface.
Wait for complete cooling and settled pressure before unscrewing or cleaning.
For classic aluminum Moka Express, hand wash with warm water without detergent/abrasives; no dishwasher. Do not automatically apply a roaster's coffee-cleaner suggestion to aluminum.
Stainless steel does not establish detergent/dishwasher compatibility; follow exact model/manual edition. Dry fully and store unclosed.

app_audit.finding: MOKA_POT retains defaultRatio 10, warnings below 8/above 12, FINE descriptor, null capacity, and 240–300-second targets. Geometry and loose basket fill are not encoded by those generic numbers.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Use equipment-fill semantics and pot-specific measured quantities; distinguish moka texture from machine espresso, and keep completion observational rather than a generic 4–5-minute promise.

app_audit.finding: instruction_moka_start says to heat with lid open; prep_tip_moka at line 122 says fill to the valve. The maker manual requires lid closed during use and fill at/below the valve's lower edge.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Align legacy starting copy with exact model's closed-lid requirement and explicitly say below valve's lower edge; retain no-tamping guidance. Review translations separately.

app_audit.finding: methodTimerGuidanceRes reads BrewMethod.stageGuidance resources and switches to timerReadyRes when elapsedSeconds reaches timeTargetLowS; metadata displays positive generic target times. Moka inherits ACTIVE_TIMER and the no-bloom LaunchedEffect at line 136 auto-starts at screen entry, potentially before heat application. Temperature rendering at line 808 guards both values >0, so Moka 0/0 is hidden.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Make Moka status and metadata depend on heat/flow observation, without claiming the 240-second ready threshold predicts completion. Start any observation/reference clock explicitly when heat is applied. Preserve hidden-temperature handling; no displayed 0 °C defect was established.

app_audit.finding: Recipe rows omit Moka's 0/0 temperature because both must be positive, but show ratio and time targets when positive.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve omission of unknown temperature. Replace generic ratio/time targets with pot-fill and observational guidance when implementing reviewed content.

app_audit.finding: Moka already has manual heat and observe-flow stages, critical below-valve safety and gentle-heat warning. There is no generic countdown completion in this typed plan.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve the manual stage contract and existing safety; align legacy timer copy instead of treating the typed plan as a countdown bug.

app_audit.finding: Existing Moka guidance already uses observed flow, low-to-medium heat, pale/sputter stop cues, below-valve fill, component checks, loose basket, no hot opening, cooldown and cleaning. The exact pale-color cue is app-authored observational guidance, not a verified universal maker rule.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve correct flow and pressure safeguards; qualify lid viewing by equipment manual and add model-compatible cleaning when implementing the guide.

app_audit.finding: Moka correctly returns null, with a comment explaining pot/protocol-specific output; no generic reservoir-to-cup coefficient is supported.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve fail-closed behavior. Any output estimate requires pot-specific observed calibration and a clearly labelled basis.

app_audit.finding: Legacy calculator still uses BrewMethod output semantics and an absorption/apparent-loss coefficient to calculate predictedCupVolumeG. Moka inherits WATER_IN_MINUS_ABSORPTION in BrewMethod; this is distinct from BeverageOutputEstimator's null model.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep any generic legacy predicted cup quantity out of reviewed Moka output claims; use measured pot-specific output rather than a transferable grounds-retention constant.

app_audit.finding: Comandante C40 MOKA_POT entry uses verified manufacturer 14–20-click stovetop range and standard axle/zero note; suggestedStart 17 is the app's midpoint. Decaf adaptation text elsewhere prescribes model-relative offsets; no universal Moka offset was verified here.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Retain sourced range and calibration limits, label midpoint as app selected, and do not claim transferable grinder clicks or universal decaf adjustment.

app_audit.finding: Checked current exact recipe catalog/errata and August learning-guide factual audit: Moka has no exact P1 recipe or Moka factual erratum in these files; current Moka guidance lives in the legacy catalog and typed manual plan.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Treat new content as method-specific research and preserve historical source assets. Catalog presence does not prove full everyday UI/localization support.

uncertainties: No physical brew, taste test, measured reservoir/basket quantity, exact beverage yield, device execution or localization review was performed.
Numeric doses and reservoir volumes are intentionally null in the equipment-fill baseline. The 3-cup example does not establish a universally safe milliliter fill or fixed basket mass.

First-gurgle endpoint is an explicitly app-authored adaptation using illy's published cold-start cue; Bialetti's manual describes removing when collector is full. No universal exact pale-color threshold is verified.
Bialetti support uses espresso-ground wording, but its instruction manual forbids fine espresso-machine grinding. The descriptive coarser-than-espresso guidance is supported by illy and Blue Bottle.
Blue Bottle's 345 g reservoir is approximate for its 6-cup example; safe actual valve fill overrides that number. Its hot-water tip does not state an exact temperature or guarantee a finish time.

Venus mirrored manufacturer manual permits dishwasher while current Bialetti Philippines product page forbids it; unresolved edition/region difference. Follow supplied exact manual; use water hand washing while unresolved.

Bialetti manual landing URL https://www.bialetti.com/it_en/manuals returned an internal fetch error; original manufacturer instruction sheet hosted by Amazon was successfully read. PDF screenshot failed, so no unextracted numeric fill table was relied upon.
Darkwoods moka PDF URL https://darkwoodscoffee.co.uk/guides/moka-pot-brew-guide.pdf returned an internal fetch error; it is not used as verified recipe evidence.

illy Australia's moka page has an erroneous French Press Instructions heading above a clearly moka-specific cold-start sequence; its actual instruction text was read, and unsupported pressure/history claims were not adopted.
Exact click calibration beyond stated standard Comandante axle/zero and a universal decaf Moka grind or timing adjustment were not verified.
do_not_claim: A universal 1:10 coffee-to-water mass ratio for moka pots.
Every moka pot finishes in 240–300 seconds or exactly 180–360 seconds.
Moka 0/0 temperature sentinel is visibly displayed as 0 °C in checked UI.
The typed Moka stage plan completes automatically by generic countdown.
Reservoir input equals collected beverage or all reservoir water must be forced through.
Grams and milliliters are interchangeable exact quantities.
Moka grounds should be machine-espresso fine or tamped.
Hot-water start is the Bialetti cold-fill manufacturer procedure.
All moka pots should be heated with lids open.
All stainless pots are dishwasher safe or all coffee cleaners are aluminum compatible.
Brikka, electric moka and classic Moka Express share one identical procedure.
A fixed C40 midpoint, transferable grinder setting or decaf timing shortcut guarantees good extraction.
Research/arithmetic checks establish a kitchen test, measured yield, release readiness or reviewed translation.
